origins.section: gurobipy Solves the Hierarchy Natively, and Its Priorities Run the Other Way
MathOpt Stores the Hierarchy in the Model, and Every Runner Solver Refuses It
Solve Each Pass to a Zero Gap, or the Gap Becomes a Tolerance

recorded.prompt:q-priority-direction: Read the whole lesson page, then this question. Using only what the page states, which option does the page decide is correct? Quote or cite the deciding passage.
recorded.outcome:q-priority-direction: "The highest priority goes first. Gurobi's documentation: one pass per distinct priority, in decreasing order." Service has priority 1, cost has 0, so service goes first.
recorded.prompt:q-runner: Read the whole lesson page, then this question. Using only what the page states, which option does the page decide is correct? Quote or cite the deciding passage.
recorded.outcome:q-runner: "What does run is lesson 4.3.2's solve_in_order ... solves them one at a time". The manual passes run "yes, any MIP solver"; each pass's kept row applies the tolerance.
recorded.prompt:q-gap: Read the whole lesson page, then this question. Using only what the page states, which option does the page decide is correct? Quote or cite the deciding passage.
recorded.outcome:q-gap: "The gap acted as a tolerance of unknown size"; "Pass 2 then gave up $162k of NPV ... a trade nobody asked for."
